name: protocol-whitelist
description: Iran's 'heavy mode': only UDP/53 and TCP/80+443 leave the network, and a TCP flow must BEGIN like TLS (record type 0x16) or HTTP (a request verb) — anything else is silently dropped from its first data packet on. QUIC is gone with the rest of UDP. Only a family that is real TLS on 443 survives.
analogue: The protocol whitelist of the June 2025 Twelve-Day War and the January 2026 blackout (Bock et al. 2020; IRBlock, USENIX Sec 2025): flows must start with a DNS/HTTP/TLS signature, 'this is what killed OpenVPN, WireGuard, IKEv2, obfs4, Hysteria and most QUIC'. Model: first-data-packet prefix test + port/protocol rules. It does NOT model the destination allow-list that the later 'whitelist new normal' adds on top (under that, no foreign VPS is reachable at all: see total-blackout), nor any entropy or fingerprint classifier.
